PullRequest.Title: Remove image preview in favor of core image previewer
PullRequest.Body:

This helps reduce duplication across image carousel and the image preview extension

The built-in `media-preview` extension is removed. Its image, video and audio previews now live in core under `src/vs/workbench/contrib/mediaPreview`:

- **Shared `ImageViewer`**: zoom, a context menu and Copy. Used by both the new core image editor and the image carousel, so the carousel now has a context menu.
- **Image editor**: reloads on file changes, including changes reported by extension file systems. Supports view state, Save As, the Git LFS pointer message, and status bar zoom, dimensions and file size. The status bar also follows the focused side of media diffs.
- **Audio and video**: rendered in a webview editor, because the workbench CSP doesn't allow `blob:` media sources.
- **Copy**: PNG sources are copied as is. Other formats are encoded in a worker, with a main-thread fallback, which keeps the fix for the delayed copy from #341783. Desktop writes through a new `IClipboardService.writeImage`, because the workbench window can't use `clipboard-sanitized-write`. Copy works with Cmd/Ctrl+C through the copy command and the browser's native `copy` event.
- **Compatibility**: the editor IDs `imagePreview.previewEditor`, `vscode.videoPreview` and `vscode.audioPreview` are kept, and editors restored from the old custom editor are migrated.

## How to test

1. Open PNG, JPEG, SVG, video and audio files. Check zoom, the context menu, Copy (including Cmd/Ctrl+C) and the status bar.
2. Compare two images and click each side. The status bar should follow the focused side.
3. Open the image carousel in the Agents window. Check the context menu and Copy, and navigate quickly between images.
4. Change an open image on disk. The preview should reload.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: passed
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- Hygiene pre-commit hook: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot` with the 5 `mediaPreview` test files and the 2 `imageCarousel` test files: 40 passing
- Manual check in Code OSS: image/video/audio previews, Copy, and the image diff status bar

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The worker call and transport's transfer-list construction are explicit, and the removed code explicitly transferred the same bitmap. The trigger is every non-PNG Copy action; only the exact browser serialization duration varies.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Decoded RGBA bitmap pixels serialized from the renderer main thread to the image encoder worker
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The transfer cost scales with pixel area (roughly width × height × 4 bytes), not compressed file size; repeated copies repeat the allocation, and high-resolution photos can require tens or hundreds of megabytes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher copy latency and a large transient memory/CPU spike while copying non-PNG images, with increased GC/OOM risk for high-resolution images.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The deleted image-preview implementation posted the ImageBitmap with worker.postMessage(bitmap, [bitmap]), transferring ownership without cloning its pixel payload.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new implementation passes ImageBitmap as a regular argument to worker.proxy.$encodePng. WebWorkerProtocol._send only adds top-level ArrayBuffer arguments to its transfer list, so the ImageBitmap is structured-cloned instead of transferred before the worker encodes it.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 620 replaces the deleted direct `worker.postMessage(bitmap, [bitmap])` call with an RPC call whose transport cannot transfer ImageBitmap objects.
Findings.Title: Transfer the bitmap to the encoder worker
Findings.Impact: Copying a typical JPEG/WebP photo now clones the full decoded bitmap between main thread and worker before PNG encoding. For an 8K image this is about 132 MiB of pixel data, on top of the canvas/worker encode allocations, delaying the Copy operation and sharply increasing peak memory.
Findings.Evidence: Added line 620 sends bitmap through the generic web-worker proxy. The unchanged WebWorkerProtocol transfer collection checks only `arg instanceof ArrayBuffer`; it never adds ImageBitmap. The removed implementation explicitly included the bitmap in postMessage's transfer list, proving the prior path avoided this serialization copy.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a worker call path that accepts an explicit transferable list (or a dedicated Worker/MessagePort) and include the ImageBitmap, preserving the existing ArrayBuffer transfer for the encoded response. Add a transport-level test that observes the transferred bitmap rather than the current in-process mock.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after paths and buffer aggregation are directly visible in the diff and file-service/webview implementations. Exact milliseconds depend on image size and provider speed, but the new O(file-size) renderer allocation and full-transfer-before-decode critical path are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Encoded image bytes in renderer memory, Blob backing storage, remote/local filesystem stream chunks, and decoded image pixels
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Peak memory and time-to-first-decode grow linearly with the encoded file size; image diffs and multiple visible previews can incur this concurrently, and every file-change reload repeats it.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased preview latency plus renderer memory/GC pressure, with large or remote images needing the entire payload materialized before decoding can begin.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The removed image-preview webview assigned the webview resource URI directly to the img element. That resource path is served by loadLocalResource via IFileService.readFileStream and forwarded chunk-by-chunk (including over the remote filesystem IPC stream), so the workbench did not aggregate the complete encoded image into a VSBuffer before browser loading.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new editor awaits IFileService.readFile for the complete image, then _showImage constructs a Blob from that full buffer and only then starts img.decode(). IFileService.readFile explicitly consumes its source stream through streamToBuffer, so this moves full-file aggregation onto the preview-open and reload critical path.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 209 is the newly introduced full-file read on the image editor's setInput critical path; the deleted implementation supplied the resource URL to img.src and relied on the existing streaming webview loader.
Findings.Title: Keep image preview loading streamed
Findings.Impact: Opening or reloading a large screenshot/photo, especially from vscode-remote or an extension filesystem, now waits for all bytes to cross the filesystem boundary and be concatenated before the browser can load it. During Blob creation the renderer can hold both the aggregated encoded buffer and Blob backing bytes in addition to the decoded bitmap; an image diff doubles the same pattern.
Findings.Evidence: Added line 209 invokes readFile on every ImagePreviewEditor load; fileService.doReadFile converts readFileStream to a complete buffer with streamToBuffer. Added line 254 then wraps that buffer in a Blob before ImageViewer.setSource begins decode. By contrast, the deleted extension created an asWebviewUri src, and unchanged webview resource loading uses readFileStream and forwards a transferable ReadableStream/chunks to the webview.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve resource-backed/streamed loading for display (for example, a narrowly scoped resource URL or streaming response path), and acquire encoded bytes separately only when Copy actually needs them. Keep cancellation and reload generation checks so superseded streams are stopped.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reload an image preview, including both sides of an image diff and remote/extension-backed resources
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setInput waits for Git-LFS detection where applicable, then the newly added full IFileService.readFile, Blob creation, and Image.decode before the preview is shown. Reloads are delayed/coalesced by 100 ms but still repeat this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the entire encoded image through IFileService.readFile, which consumes and concatenates its source stream
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One complete read per initial open and per scheduled reload, or two concurrent reads for an image diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed custom editor set img.src to a webview resource URI; webview resource loading used IFileService.readFileStream and forwarded chunks/transferable stream data instead of aggregating a full workbench buffer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The complete read and concatenation must finish before Blob creation and image decoding can begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remote filesystem chunks cross the remote filesystem channel; the new readFile path aggregates them in the renderer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stream per image read, with chunk count proportional to file size
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same remote stream fed the webview resource response incrementally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All remote chunks must now arrive and be concatenated before decode starts.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Encoded image byte size; one load per visible preview side, repeated per coalesced file-change burst. Side-by-side diffs can run two image loads concurrently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each pane loads independently. A RunOnceScheduler coalesces file events within 100 ms, but already-started reload reads are not canceled; generation IDs only suppress stale presentation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No byte cache exists for ImagePreviewEditor. The current Blob/object URL is retained only for the displayed image and revoked on replacement/clear. Every reload re-reads all bytes; Git-LFS checks are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed call path reaches readFile -> streamToBuffer, followed by Blob construction and decode; the old path reaches the streaming webview resource loader.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact memory peak and latency depend on compressed size, decoded dimensions, provider speed, and whether Blob construction copies backing storage, but full-buffer aggregation and full-transfer-before-decode are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: the new editor replaces streaming display with eager full-file aggregation on the open/reload critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copy the displayed image from the image preview or carousel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PNG sources are read and validated, then written to the clipboard. Other formats are drawn into a full-resolution OffscreenCanvas, converted to ImageBitmap, sent to the encoder worker, encoded as PNG, returned as an ArrayBuffer, and finally written through browser clipboard or desktop native-host IPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send ImageBitmap through generic web-worker RPC without including it in the transfer list
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-resolution bitmap serialization per non-PNG Copy
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted implementation called worker.postMessage(bitmap, [bitmap]) and transferred ownership zero-copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The bitmap must be serialized/cloned before worker encoding can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send encoded PNG bytes from renderer to Electron main and write via Electron clipboard
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC payload per Copy on desktop, proportional to encoded PNG size
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The extension wrote through navigator.clipboard inside the webview, so this native-host IPC boundary was absent; it replaces browser clipboard access for core workbench compatibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Clipboard completion awaits the IPC write after encoding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser ClipboardItem write for web builds
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed extension also used navigator.clipboard.write once per Copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Clipboard completion awaits promised PNG bytes and browser clipboard write.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Decoded pixel area for non-PNG images (approximately width x height x 4), and compressed PNG byte size for PNG pass-through and clipboard IPC.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each Copy invocation creates a new worker client and encode. There is no coalescing or shared limiter, so repeated Copy invocations can overlap, though normal usage is one user-triggered operation at a time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The displayed Blob is retained by the viewer/editor, avoiding a filesystem reread. Encoded PNG results are not cached. Worker clients are disposed after each encode.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: WebWorkerProtocol only transfers top-level ArrayBuffer arguments, and the changed call supplies ImageBitmap.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific structured-clone implementation affects exact copy duration, but the RPC transfer list definitively excludes ImageBitmap while the prior code explicitly transferred it. High-resolution photos make the pixel cardinality large.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: non-PNG Copy loses the prior transferable ImageBitmap path and adds full-pixel serialization/allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigate quickly through image carousel entries, including adjacent preloading and videos
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Current image bytes are loaded or reused from the Blob cache, decoded asynchronously, then shown; metadata/thumbnail state updates immediately and adjacent entries are preloaded off the direct navigation completion path. Videos read their bytes and post one transferred ArrayBuffer into a lazily created webview.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read URI-backed current and adjacent media files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful read per unique uncached image ID, plus up to two adjacent preloads per navigation that hit cache after first success
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The carousel already read URI-backed media and preloaded adjacent entries before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The current image read is on the navigation critical path; adjacent preloads are fire-and-forget.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post transferred video ArrayBuffer into carousel webview
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This video postMessage path is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after the full video read and is required for playback.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and byte size of distinct images visited or adjacent-preloaded; effective cache cardinality is unique image IDs in the current carousel generation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Current load plus up to two adjacent preloads may run concurrently. Rapid navigation can start independent per-image reads, but generation/index checks suppress stale presentation; concurrent same-ID results are deduplicated only after one completes, not coalesced in flight.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Blob/object URLs are cached per image ID for the carousel lifetime and all are revoked on input replacement/clear. The diff retains the Blob alongside its URL for Copy, but an object URL already keeps the Blob backing data alive, so this does not establish extra retained encoded bytes. No negative cache exists for failed/missing images.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary counts/cache lifecycle; moderate for the magnitude of the added layout probe.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A new intrinsic-width probe appends a hidden element and synchronously reads geometry after decode, but only the winning current source reaches it; evidence is insufficient that one isolated probe creates a material user-visible regression beyond the reported issues.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: filesystem/preload fan-out and cache lifetime are materially unchanged, and the added one-per-winning-image layout probe lacks sufficient impact evidence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, restore, hide, or reload audio/video previews
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolver/input creation is lightweight and overlay webviews are lazy until claimed. Resolve renders HTML after an optional Git-LFS check; the browser then streams the media resource. File-size stat runs asynchronously after HTML is set and is not on playback startup's direct await chain.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Git-LFS stat and optional small pointer read
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for non-git media; one stat and at most one <=1 KiB read per render for git resources
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed extension performed the same Git-LFS check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before setting webview HTML for git resources only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stream audio/video resource through the webview resource loader
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One media stream per load/reload, with range requests controlled by the browser
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed media webviews used the same resource URI/resource loader behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Feeds playback incrementally after HTML is installed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat media for status-bar file size
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The extension also issued a separate stat for binary-size status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Launched after webview HTML is set and not awaited by _render, so it is off the media-render critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One media resource per editor; restored hidden editors create overlay wrappers but not underlying webview elements. Git resources at most add one stat and a <=1 KiB pointer read.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Editors resolve independently. File changes are coalesced for 100 ms per input; retained hidden webviews preserve playback state as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser/webview media caching applies. Cache-busting query changes on reload when the source URI has no existing query. No application-level media byte cache is added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying browser buffering and codec behavior vary by media type; boundary cardinality and scheduling are clear.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: media streaming, retained hidden context, and size-stat behavior preserve the prior architecture and do not add scaling boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and migration of legacy media-preview custom editors
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution module is imported with workbench startup; resolver registrations happen at BlockStartup. After restoration, migration scans restored editors and replaces only legacy media previews, grouping replacements by editor group.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace restored legacy editors through IEditorService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One replaceEditors call per affected editor group, each batching that group's legacy tabs
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No migration pass was needed while the extension remained installed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs at AfterRestored, not before basic workbench restoration can progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total restored editor count for the scan and number of legacy media tabs for replacement; both are bounded by the user's restored session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Replacement is invoked once per affected group without awaiting across groups; there is no explicit limiter, but realistic group counts are small and this runs once after restore.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; migration is a one-time restored-session compatibility pass.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for scan/replacement placement, low for material startup impact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Module parse/registration adds startup code, but the contribution is modest and the migration is one-time, grouped, and post-restore; no concrete material startup symptom is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: migration work is bounded, grouped by editor group, and intentionally after restoration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Save As and status-bar/focus updates for media previews
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Save As waits for a user-selected destination and one file-service copy. Focus/status changes update context keys and at most three status entries synchronously with no filesystem work on focus.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy media file to selected destination
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One copy per confirmed Save As
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The extension-backed readonly custom editor did not expose this core Save As implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The Save As operation waits for the copy, as required.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source file per Save As; one active pane and three status entries per focus/image-info change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: User-triggered Save As operations are independent; status updates are synchronous and constant-cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Copy duration scales with source size/provider speed, but it is explicit user-requested work with no avoidable amplification.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: one filesystem copy is necessary for Save As, and status/focus updates remain constant-time without expensive boundaries.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full changed-file inventory and relevant diff pages. Two introduced regressions were submitted: eager full-file buffering on image open/reload, and loss of transferable ImageBitmap semantics on non-PNG worker encoding. Other startup, media streaming, carousel cache/preload, status, save, cleanup, and concurrency paths were traced without additional high-confidence regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
